title: Richard Nixon resignation after Watergate
trigger: The Watergate scandal involved the break-in at the Democratic National Committee headquarters and the subsequent cover-up by the Nixon administration, leading to Nixon's resignation before impeachment.

timeline.event: Five burglars arrested at Democratic National Committee headquarters in the Watergate complex
Nixon announces his resignation, effective August 9
Gerald Ford sworn in as 38th President of the United States
Gerald Ford grants Nixon a full pardon

outcome.summary: Richard Nixon resigned the presidency on August 9, 1974, facing near-certain impeachment over the Watergate scandal. Gerald Ford succeeded him and granted Nixon a full pardon one month later. The scandal led to reforms in campaign finance, government ethics, and congressional oversight.

claims.text: Five burglars were arrested at the Democratic National Committee headquarters in the Watergate complex on June 17, 1972
The Senate Watergate Committee began hearings on July 13, 1973
Richard Nixon announced his resignation on August 8, 1974, effective August 9
Gerald Ford was sworn in as 38th President on August 9, 1974
Gerald Ford granted Richard Nixon a full pardon on September 8, 1974
